{"id": "d767c4a9-287d-48b1-b730-4bfdca315967", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_61foMNQeaDg6WxsywYaDcm", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"## Note on ask_user usage\\\\n\\\\nEvery `ask_user` call in this skill resolves input required for the next tool call \\\\u2014 target recommendation (Step 1), reason category (Step 2), subcategory (Step 3), or Submit/Cancel confirmation (Step 4 of refine). These are real disambiguations, not follow-ups.\\\\n\\\\nDo **not** add extra `ask_user` calls after ACCEPT/REJECT/REFINE completes. Close in prose. No \\\\\"anything else?\\\\\" menus.\\\\n\\\\n## Viewing and Listing\\\\n\\\\n## Analyzing Patterns\\\\n\\\\nWhen users ask about patterns or trends across recommendations (e.g., \\\\\"What patterns do you see?\\\\\" on the prevention page), use `list_recommendations` to fetch recommendations and analyze them for:\\\\n- Common root causes or affected services\\\\n- Severity distribution\\\\n- Recurring resource types or categories\\\\n- Trends over time\\\\n\\\\nPresent your analysis as actionable insights, not just raw data.\\\\n\\\\n## Accepting a Recommendation\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user wants to accept a recommendation, follow this flow.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1: Identify Target Recommendation\\\\n\\\\nDetermine which recommendation the user is referring to:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Page context**: If `[now viewing: /recommendation/rec-<uuid>]` is present, use the recommendation ID from the URL\\\\n2. **Conversation context**: If a recommendation was recently discussed, infer it and confirm with the user\\\\n3. **Search**: If ambiguous, call `list_recommendations` with `limit: 4` and call `ask_user` to let the user select:\\\\n   ```\\\\n   ask_user(\\\\n     question=\\\\\"Which recommendation would you like to accept?\\\\\",\\\\n     options=[\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"<title_1>\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"<brief summary>\\\\\"},\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"<title_2>\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"<brief summary>\\\\\"},\\\\n       ...\\\\n     ]\\\\n   )\\\\n   ```\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2: Submit\\\\n\\\\nCall `update_recommendation(action=ACCEPT, recommendation_id=...)`. Report the result to the user.\\\\n\\\\n## Rejecting a Recommendation\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user wants to reject a recommendation, follow this flow.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1: Identify Target and Fetch Details\\\\n\\\\nDetermine which recommendation the user is referring to (using page context, conversation context, or search as described above). Call `get_recommendation` to fetch full details. Optionally call `get_recommendation_investigation_overview` with the same `recommendation_id` to retrieve investigation context \\\\u2014 the incident groups analyzed, research questions asked, and candidate fixes evaluated. If it returns an error or empty data, proceed without it.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2: Understand the Issue\\\\n\\\\nCall `ask_user` to determine the rejection reason:\\\\n```\\\\nask_user(\\\\n  question=\\\\\"What\\'s the issue with this recommendation?\\\\\",\\\\n  options=[\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Wrong analysis\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The problem identification, root cause, or incident grouping is incorrect\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Wrong fix\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The proposed solution won\\'t work or isn\\'t the best approach\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Not relevant\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"This recommendation doesn\\'t apply to our situation or is no longer needed\\\\\"}\\\\n  ]\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIf the user provides free-text that doesn\\'t match exactly, map it to the closest category and confirm your interpretation.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 3: Gather Details\\\\n\\\\nBased on the selected category, ask targeted follow-up questions to understand the specific issue. Use investigation context (if available) to make questions more specific \\\\u2014 reference actual research questions, incident groups, or candidate evaluations rather than asking only generic questions. If the user doesn\\'t want to provide details, that\\'s fine \\\\u2014 details are optional for rejection.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 4: Suggest Refinement\\\\n\\\\nIf the user\\'s feedback is actionable (e.g., they identified a better fix, a correct root cause, or missing context), call `ask_user`:\\\\n```\\\\nask_user(\\\\n  question=\\\\\"Would you like a refined recommendation incorporating your feedback, or just reject it?\\\\\",\\\\n  options=[\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Refine\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Generate a refined recommendation with your feedback\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Reject\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Reject without refinement\\\\\"}\\\\n  ]\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n- If the user selects \\\\\"Refine\\\\\", redirect to the **Refining a Recommendation** flow (skip directly to Step 4 since you already have the category and details)\\\\n- If the user selects \\\\\"Reject\\\\\", proceed to Step 5\\\\n\\\\n### Step 5: Submit\\\\n\\\\nCall `update_recommendation(action=REJECT, recommendation_id=..., reason_category=..., details=...)` directly. The user already expressed intent to reject (either explicitly or by choosing Reject in Step 4). Include reason_category and details if the user provided them; omit if not. Report the result to the user.\\\\n\\\\n## Refining a Recommendation\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user wants to refine or improve a recommendation (triggering re-generation with their feedback), follow this flow.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1: Identify Target and Fetch Details\\\\n\\\\nDetermine which recommendation the user is referring to (using page context, conversation context, or search as described above). Call `get_recommendation` to fetch full details. Check the `status` field before proceeding:\\\\n\\\\n- If `ACCEPTED`: inform the user the recommendation has already been accepted. Offer alternative paths if appropriate.\\\\n- If `CLOSED` or `COMPLETED`: inform the user it\\'s finalized and cannot be refined.\\\\n- Only proceed to Step 2 if status is `PROPOSED` or `REJECTED`.\\\\n\\\\nCall `get_recommendation_investigation_overview` with the same `recommendation_id` to retrieve investigation context \\\\u2014 the incident groups analyzed, research questions asked, and candidate fixes evaluated. If it returns an error or empty data, proceed without it.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2: Gather Reason Category\\\\n\\\\nIf not already known (e.g., redirected from the reject flow), call `ask_user` to determine the category:\\\\n```\\\\nask_user(\\\\n  question=\\\\\"What\\'s the issue with this recommendation?\\\\\",\\\\n  options=[\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Wrong analysis\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The problem identification, root cause, or incident grouping is incorrect\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Wrong fix\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The proposed solution won\\'t work or isn\\'t the best approach\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Not relevant\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"This recommendation doesn\\'t apply to our situation or is no longer needed\\\\\"}\\\\n  ]\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIf the user provides free-text that doesn\\'t match exactly, map it to the closest category and confirm your interpretation.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 3: Gather Detailed Feedback\\\\n\\\\nBased on the selected category, call `ask_user` with targeted follow-up options. Examples:\\\\n\\\\n**WRONG_ANALYSIS:**\\\\n```\\\\nask_user(\\\\n  question=\\\\\"What specifically is wrong with the analysis?\\\\\",\\\\n  options=[\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Wrong root cause\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The root cause analysis is wrong\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Bad grouping\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The incidents aren\\'t related or are grouped incorrectly\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Missing context\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Missing context led to an incorrect conclusion\\\\\"}\\\\n  ]\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n**WRONG_FIX:**\\\\n```\\\\nask_user(\\\\n  question=\\\\\"What\\'s wrong with the proposed fix?\\\\\",\\\\n  options=[\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Won\\'t solve it\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The fix won\\'t solve the problem\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Better alternative\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"There\\'s a better alternative approach\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Bad trade-offs\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The fix has unacceptable trade-offs or side effects\\\\\"}\\\\n  ]\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n**NOT_RELEVANT:**\\\\n```\\\\nask_user(\\\\n  question=\\\\\"Why isn\\'t this recommendation relevant?\\\\\",\\\\n  options=[\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Already resolved\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Already resolved or addressed through a different approach\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Decommissioned\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"The resource has been decommissioned or the infrastructure has changed\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Expected behavior\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"This is expected behavior for our setup\\\\\"}\\\\n  ]\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIf the user types a free-text response, ask a follow-up if the answer is too vague to get actionable detail.\\\\n\\\\n**Using investigation context**: If the investigation overview is available, use it to make your follow-up questions more specific. Reference the actual research questions, incident groups, or candidate evaluations from the investigation rather than asking only generic questions.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 4: Confirm Summary\\\\n\\\\nSummarize the collected feedback for the user in prose:\\\\n\\\\n- **Recommendation**: [title of the recommendation]\\\\n- **Issue**: [reason category]\\\\n- **Details**: [summary of their feedback and clarifications]\\\\n\\\\nThe user has already expressed intent to refine and provided the feedback. Do **not** call `ask_user` to re-confirm submission \\\\u2014 that is permission-gating. Proceed directly to Step 5. If the user wants to correct the summary, they can say so in a follow-up turn.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 5: Submit\\\\n\\\\nCall `update_recommendation(action=REFINE, recommendation_id=..., reason_category=..., details=...)`. Report the result to the user, explaining that a refined recommendation will be generated based on their feedback.\\\\n\\\\n## Priority Preferences\\\\n\\\\nIf the customer volunteers priority signals during a recommendation interaction, continue the recommendation workflow normally -- the `ranking-preferences` skill handles preference collection independently.\\\\n\\\\n## Terminology\\\\n\\\\nAlways refer to these as \\\\\"Recommendations\\\\\" when talking to users. Frame interactions naturally: \\\\\"accept\\\\\", \\\\\"reject\\\\\", or \\\\\"refine/improve\\\\\" rather than technical terms like \\\\\"updating status\\\\\" or \\\\\"submitting a reason category\\\\\".\"}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}
